changes.summary: Waiver claims work again during the waiver window — every claim was being refused as "player locked", and Free Agents offers Add on every free agent again.
Maverick's 2016–2024 seasons show their original Mel Gibson art again instead of today's logo, and it's now Maverick's default Throwback Week look.
The player card's Season Results table is readable again — upcoming weeks and byes no longer vanish in dark mode, and it fits a phone without scrolling sideways.
Declaring a contract works again — it was failing with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cancelled')" and never filed.
The rest of the player card's faded labels (stats, details, section titles, "Rostered by") are now easy to read in both light and dark mode.
On a phone, Coach view roster cards keep the matchup and the stats line on one line each — a 10:00 kickoff or a two-digit rank no longer bumps the rank or the average onto a line of its own.
Live Scoring: Throwback teams now wear their era colours, and when two teams share a colour your own team keeps it.
Live Scoring: during Throwback Week, a team wearing an old name shows its current name in small print underneath, so you can still tell who's who.
Schefter: the weekly waiver column now knows a first-come free-agent pickup still signs at the $425K league minimum — it is never "free".
Franchise and rivalry trade ledgers: pre-2011 trades now name every player instead of "Player #6955", and each team appears under the name it had that season.
Draft Results: defenses show their NFL team logo, and players with no photo get a silhouette instead of a broken image.
Lineup alerts now go out before every kickoff, London and Thursday games included, and never name a player whose game has already started.
The featured player on every roster header now gets the Free Agents spotlight treatment: a big headshot over his NFL team's logo in white.
Rosters: each position group now has its own band with a running total that follows your sort, and All players ranks your whole roster by any column.
changes.headline: Rosters, sorted your way
changes.lede: Position bands make every group easy to scan, and any column now sorts — inside each group, or across your whole roster with All players.
changes.imageAlt: The Rosters table with a Quarterbacks band and a Running backs band, each showing its projected-points total, under a Grouped / All players toggle

changes.summary: Rosters: switching from Coach back to GM no longer leaves the Coach columns showing until you toggle twice.
Rosters: sorting right after switching teams no longer swaps in the previous team's players.
Rosters: the table no longer scrolls sideways on narrower desktop windows when every column fits.
After switching teams from the roster header's crest row, the browser's Back button now returns to the team you came from instead of the one the page first opened on.
